stem.text: Let \( f(x) = \frac{- 2 x^{2} + 10 x - 12}{x^{2} - 4 x + 3} \). Find every vertical asymptote of the graph of f, and state the one sided limits of f at each one.

answer_key.label: Only \( x = 1 \) is a vertical asymptote, with \( \lim_{x \to 1^{-}} f(x) = -\infty \) and \( \lim_{x \to 1^{+}} f(x) = \infty \).

worked_solution.text: Factor and cancel: for \( x \ne 3 \), \( f(x) = \frac{4 - 2 x}{x - 1} \). The factor at \( x = 3 \) divides out, so that break is removable, with no asymptote.
The remaining denominator is 0 only at \( x = 1 \), where the numerator of the reduced expression is 2, not 0.
The denominator \( x - 1 \) is negative just left of 1 and positive just right of it, so \( \lim_{x \to 1^{-}} f(x) = -\infty \) and \( \lim_{x \to 1^{+}} f(x) = \infty \).
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the quotient on each side

options.label: Both \( x = 3 \) and \( x = 1 \) are vertical asymptotes, with \( \lim_{x \to 1^{-}} f(x) = -\infty \) and \( \lim_{x \to 1^{+}} f(x) = \infty \).
options.derivation: a vertical asymptote named at the zero of the denominator whose factor divides out

options.label: No line is a vertical asymptote, because \( \lim_{x \to 1^{+}} f(x) = \infty \) is a limit that exists at \( x = 1 \).
options.derivation: the infinite one sided limit read as an existing limit, so no asymptote is recognised

options.label: Only \( x = 1 \) is a vertical asymptote, with \( \lim_{x \to 1^{-}} f(x) = -\infty \) and \( \lim_{x \to 1^{+}} f(x) = \infty \).
Only \( x = 1 \) is a vertical asymptote, with \( \lim_{x \to 1} f(x) = \infty \) from both sides.
options.derivation: one two sided infinite limit written although the two sides have opposite signs
